The standing law of conscription. It requires men to register at 18 and maintains the Selective Service System so that a draft could be run if Congress and the President restored the power to induct.

## Key provisions

- Registration of male citizens and most male residents aged 18 through 25.
- Classification, deferment, and conscientious objector provisions.
- Local boards and a lottery system for any future induction.
- Induction authority lapsed in 1973; registration was suspended in 1975 and resumed in 1980.

## Why it matters

It is the legal basis of the all-volunteer force's backstop. Any large war would test it before it tested the [mobilization authorities](reserve-mobilization.qmd). Proposals to automate registration or extend it to women usually move through [the annual NDAA](ndaa-annual.qmd).

## Current status

The registration requirement is in force. Authority to induct expired on July 1, 1973, so a draft would require new legislation. Changes to registration have been proposed in recent defense bills. Check current status.
